item.title: Third-Party Vendor Security Incident (Klue) [resolved]
item.description: Our forensic investigation into the June 2026 Klue/Salesforce incident, conducted in partnership with Mandiant, is now complete. The investigation confirmed that the impact was limited to business CRM data. No evidence of impact to the Snyk platform, and any sensitive data within, was found. All impacted customers were notified directly and the data involved is consistent with what was disclosed in our June 22 blog post (https://snyk.io/blog/when-a-vendors-breach-becomes-yours-lessons-from-the-klue-incident/).

item.title: Snyk Code (SAST) Scan service degraded [resolved]
item.description:
The issue affecting SAST scans and API-driven automated tests has been successfully resolved, and all services have returned to normal status. Our engineering team identified the root cause as an expensive SQL query that triggered database degradation. The query has been mitigated, and performance has stabilized.
Thank you for your patience while we worked through this.

item.title: Snyk Code Degradation [resolved]
item.description:
Between 12:03 and 12:04 UTC today (1st June 2026), Snyk experienced a brief period of degradation affecting Snyk Code scans and custom Rule Extension tests. This impacted scans run via the CLI, IDE plugins, CLI uploads, as well as PR Checks.
Services have now fully recovered. Please retry any scans or tests that failed during this window.

item.title: GitHub Cloud App Integration Service Degradation [resolved]
item.description: The intermittent issues affecting repository scans, project imports, and Pull Request status checks have been fully resolved. The root cause was an upstream degradation with GitHub Cloud app installation token authentication, which has now been mitigated on the GitHub side (ref: GitHub Incident k5z4d1v1tqmt). If you continue to experience issues with your PRs, imports, or repository scans, please reach out to our support team for further assistance.
